meta.title: Lowmoor Goes Under
meta.tagline: Five school days until the reservoir swallows the town. Someone stole the speech you wrote for the last assembly.
meta.era: present day, a town that will not exist next month
meta.premise: On Saturday the floodgates close and Lowmoor becomes the bottom of a reservoir. Everyone is moving to different cities; the school is half packed into boxes. Junie Okafor-Pryce, class rep by default, has written the farewell speech for Friday's Last Assembly: the one that names every family, every shop, the swimming hole and the stupid goose. Then her notebook vanished at Monday lunch. Rosalind, her ex-best-friend, has it. And Mags Calloway, whose father sits on the Reservoir Board, has booked the Last Assembly for a sponsored 'Celebration of New Beginnings'.
meta.prompt: the last week of school before a town floods

str.name: Presence
str.description: Taking up space in a room. Volume, posture, being impossible to ignore.

dex.name: Timing
dex.description: Knowing exactly when to say it. Dodging awkward moments.

int.name: Wit
int.description: How fast and how sharp. Fuels signature moves.

hp.name: Composure
hp.description: How long you can keep it together. At zero you go home early and cry in the car.

mp.name: Nerve
mp.description: Courage in reserve. Spent on big moments.

ac.name: Poise
ac.description: How well things roll off you.

statuses.name: Flustered
statuses.description: Cheeks hot, words in the wrong order.

statuses.name: Distracted
statuses.description: Phone buzzing. Who said what? Wait, what were we doing?

statuses.name: Mortified
statuses.description: Frozen. Wishing the floor would open. It might, actually, by Saturday.

statuses.name: Written Up
statuses.description: Told to stand right there and wait. You do.

statuses.name: Seen Through
statuses.description: Someone who knows you too well just said the true thing.

statuses.name: Flash-blind
statuses.description: Purple blobs everywhere. That photo is going in the yearbook.

statuses.name: Offline
statuses.description: Dead phone. You have no idea what anyone is saying about you.

statuses.name: Hyped
statuses.description: Song in your head, bounce in your step.

statuses.name: In the Zone
statuses.description: Everything is landing. Each breath steadies you a little more.

statuses.name: Starstruck
statuses.description: Briefly convinced you are the coolest person alive.

statuses.name: Honked At
statuses.description: The goose has chosen you. Run.

resources.name: Battery
resources.description: Your phone, cracked screen and all. Apps cost charge; at zero you are offline.

onEmpty.text: Your phone dies mid-scroll. The silence is enormous.

rules.name: Small Town, Long Memory
rules.description: Every time you leave someone speechless, the group chat hears about it. Lowmoor keeps score.

effects.text: Without your phone, the hallways feel twice as long.

rules.name: The Water's Coming
rules.description: The reservoir is already seeping up through the floors. Every day, and every so often, a little more of Lowmoor goes wet.

effects.text: There is water on the floor again. Nobody mentions it.

rules.name: Three Strikes
rules.description: Hall monitors are writing people up for anything. Collect three detention slips and you are sent home for the week, and the week is all there is.

player.name: Juniper Okafor-Pryce
player.title: Class Rep (Nobody Else Ran)
player.description: Sixteen. Knows the name of every family on every street, which turns out to be a superpower nobody asked for. Has a speech to give.

perks.name: Thick Skin
perks.description: You've heard worse. From your own brother. +6 Composure, +1 Poise.

perks.name: Quick Wit
perks.description: The comeback arrives before the shower, for once. +2 Wit.

perks.name: Main Character Energy
perks.description: You walk like there's a soundtrack. +2 Presence.

perks.name: Read the Room
perks.description: You notice who's about to say something. +2 sight.

perks.name: Pep Talker
perks.description: Coach's speeches finally rubbed off. Learn Pep Talk.

perks.name: Last Word
perks.description: Getting the last word feels incredible. Recover a little Composure every time.

perks.name: Power Saver Mode
perks.description: You finally turned off background refresh. Each new day starts with extra charge.

actors.name: Group Chat Lurker
actors.description: Never says anything to your face. Screenshots everything. Travels in threes.

actors.name: Senior Prankster
actors.description: Graduating into a town that won't exist. Has decided nothing matters, loudly, at you.

actors.name: Hall Monitor
actors.description: Sash, clipboard, absolute certainty. Has been waiting four years for authority and this is the last week to use it.

abilities.name: Write-Up
abilities.description: Tears off a pink slip with your name already on it.

effects.text: A detention slip. That's one more.

actors.name: Reservoir Board Surveyor
actors.description: Hi-vis vest, laser level, a smile like a brochure. Keeps asking whether your parents have signed the buyout forms.

actors.name: Yearbook Paparazzo
actors.description: Waits behind doors with a camera. Has never taken a flattering photo in their life and considers this artistic integrity.

actors.name: The Biology Lab Goose
actors.description: Arrived in Year 7 for a project and never left. Nobody knows who feeds it. It has opinions about you specifically.

abilities.name: HONK
abilities.description: A sound that reaches the soul.

actors.name: Rosalind Achterberg
actors.description: Your best friend from age four to fourteen. Then something happened neither of you will name. She has your notebook, and she has read it.

abilities.name: Brutal Honesty
abilities.description: She says the true thing. Out loud. In front of people.

effects.text: Rosalind's voice cracks. 'It's a good speech, Junie. You put my mum's bakery in it.' She holds out the notebook.

npc.personality: Sharp, guarded, secretly devastated about moving to a city where nobody knew her at four.
npc.greeting: Looking for something? You always did leave things lying around.
lines: You wrote about the swimming hole. You wrote about me.
Everyone's leaving anyway. What's a speech going to do?
Fine. Say the thing. You always say the thing.
npc.secrets: She stole the notebook to read what Junie wrote about her, not to stop the speech.
npc.wants: An apology for Year 9, which Junie doesn't know she owes.

actors.name: Magdalena 'Mags' Calloway
actors.description: Head girl, debate champion, daughter of the Reservoir Board chair. She has a sponsor, a slideshow and a hashtag: #NewBeginnings. She will not be interrupted.

abilities.name: Devastating Read
abilities.description: A paragraph-long takedown, delivered at microphone volume.

abilities.name: Rally the Squad
abilities.description: Three phones light up at once.

abilities.name: Fix Lip Gloss
abilities.description: A compact mirror, a deep breath, total reset.

npc.personality: Polished, relentless, privately terrified that the town will blame her family forever.
npc.greeting: Junie! Love that you came. You're not on the programme, but you can clap.
lines: Change is an opportunity, not a tragedy.
Nobody wants to cry at an assembly, Juniper.
My dad didn't flood the town. Physics did.
npc.secrets: Her grandmother's house is on the list too; she has not told anyone she voted against the dam in the student poll.
npc.wants: For someone to tell her it isn't her fault.

actors.name: Mr. Abernathy-Oyelaran
actors.description: School custodian for thirty-one years. Keeper of the lost-and-found, which this week is the size of a small department store.

npc.personality: Unhurried, kind, extremely precise about mops. Trades lost property for favours, never for money.
npc.greeting: Ah. Okafor-Pryce. You'll want the lost-and-found. Everybody wants the lost-and-found this week.
lines: Thirty-one years. Never once found a left shoe and a right shoe that matched.
The goose? Leave the goose alone.
Water's in the boiler room again. Doesn't matter now, I suppose.
npc.secrets: He has the school's old 1961 yearbook and knows Nan Ottoline was the last person to give a farewell speech in Lowmoor, when the old village went under.
npc.wants: Someone to take the trophy case photographs before the water does.

actors.name: Priya Dass
actors.description: Drama club, every play, every year. Has decided this week is a tragedy in five acts and she is going to give it her all.

npc.personality: Theatrical, loyal, quotes plays nobody has read, cries easily and recovers instantly.
npc.greeting: Junie! Exeunt, pursued by a goose! Where are we going?
lines: Every great speech is stolen at least once. It's tradition.
If anyone makes you cry, I will cry louder.
Is this the third act? It feels like the third act.
npc.secrets: She saw Rosalind reading the notebook on the bus, crying.
npc.wants: To be part of something people will remember.

actors.name: Coach Wendeline Strand
actors.description: PE teacher, swimming coach, lifeguard at the old swimming hole for twenty summers. Whistle permanently around her neck.

npc.personality: Booming, sentimental, believes any problem can be solved by hydration and a lap.
npc.greeting: OKAFOR-PRYCE! Water bottle. Deep breath. Tell Coach.
lines: Shoulders back. Chin up. You've got this.
Twenty summers I watched that swimming hole. Not one drowning. And now look.
Drink something. Not that. Water.
npc.secrets: She is moving into a flat with no window. She hasn't told her swimmers.
npc.wants: To hear the swimming hole mentioned at the assembly.

actors.name: Theo Marsh
actors.description: Year 8. Knows everything about everyone, mostly from standing very still in corridors. Bolts at loud noises.

npc.personality: Whispers. Exact. Slightly unsettling. Wants to be useful more than anything.
npc.greeting: Psst. I know where your notebook is. I also know where the goose sleeps.
lines: Rosalind's having a party Wednesday. Her house is half boxes.
Hall monitors only write you up if you stop moving.
Mags practised her speech in the empty pool. It echoed. She cried a bit.
npc.secrets: He knows the hall monitors' detention slips can be erased with the janitor's special eraser.
npc.wants: To be mentioned in the speech. Just once. 'Theo Marsh, who knew things.'

actors.name: Nan Ottoline
actors.description: Class of 1961. Gave the farewell speech when the OLD village went under the first reservoir. Has come back for the second one.

npc.personality: Tiny, funny, unsentimental about everything except names. Remembers every family that was lost the first time.
npc.greeting: You're the one with the speech. Good. Read me the first line. No, louder.
lines: We lost the first village in 1961. I said every name. It took eleven minutes. Nobody left.
Don't make it pretty. Make it true.
The water doesn't care. That's why you have to.
npc.secrets: Her own speech was cut short by the then-chair of the Reservoir Board: Mags Calloway's great-grandfather.
npc.wants: To hear the old village named alongside the new.

items.name: Dog-eared Thesaurus
items.description: Fourteen synonyms for 'devastated' are highlighted. Always the right word, eventually.

items.name: Drama Club Megaphone
items.description: Red, dented, smells of stage paint. Makes anything you say sound like an announcement.

items.name: Permanent Marker of Truth
items.description: Used to sign every cast in Lowmoor for a decade. Write the true thing where everyone can read it.

items.name: Thrift-Store Blazer
items.description: Two sizes too big, elbow patches, smells faintly of someone else's grandad. You look like you mean it.

items.name: Borrowed Varsity Jacket
items.description: Somebody's brother's, from the year Lowmoor won the county. Instantly gives you the walk.

items.name: Lucky Scrunchie
items.description: Velvet, faded teal. Worn for every exam since Year 7. Undefeated.

items.name: Noise-Cancelling Headphones
items.description: The world gets quieter. Insults lose their edge. So does everything else.

effects.text: The hallway noise rushes back in like water.

items.name: Cracked Phone
items.description: Spiderweb screen, sticker case, 40% of the time it works every time. Opens the map app.

effects.text: The map loads, mostly. Half of Lowmoor is already marked as 'water'.

items.name: Group Text Blast
items.description: Send one message to everyone. Watch every phone in the room buzz at once.

items.name: Perfect Comeback
items.description: You've rehearsed it in the shower for years. Costs nerve to actually say.

items.name: Pep Talk
items.description: Shoulders back, chin up, and tell everybody nearby - including yourself - that they've got this.

items.name: Power Bank
items.description: Somebody's sticker-covered brick of borrowed electricity.

items.name: Vending Machine Iced Tea
items.description: Peach flavour. The vending machine is the only thing in school still fully stocked.

items.name: Rosalind's Old Mixtape
items.description: A real cassette. Side A: 'SUMMER'. Side B: 'DO NOT LISTEN WITHOUT ME'. Three good plays left in the tape.

items.name: Inside Joke
items.description: Only works once. Only works on one person. Absolutely destroys them.

items.name: The Janitor's Special Eraser
items.description: Grey, pumice-hard, rumoured to remove anything from any official form.

effects.text: One detention slip, gently erased into history.

items.name: Laminated Hall Pass
items.description: Signed by a teacher who left in March. Nobody questions a laminated hall pass.

effects.text: You wave the pass. Corridors part like the Red Sea.

items.name: Cafeteria Cookie
items.description: Made by Mrs. Pell, whose recipe goes under the water with the rest of the town. Still warm.

items.name: Lightning Lemon Energy
items.description: Banned in two countries. You can feel it in your teeth.

items.name: Gas Station Sushi
items.description: Bought on Tuesday. It is no longer Tuesday.

effects.text: That was a mistake, and your stomach would like a word.

items.name: Secret Admirer Note
items.description: 'Your speech is going to be the best thing anyone says about this town. - ?'

items.name: Burn Book Page
items.description: A torn page of everyone's secrets in four colours of gel pen. Reading it tells you a lot, and costs you something.

effects.text: Now you know what everything is. And what everyone thinks.

items.name: Polaroid of the Swimming Hole
items.description: Summer, years ago. Everyone in it is laughing at something just out of frame.
items.vagueText: Looking at it makes your chest ache in a way that somehow helps.

items.name: Lowmoor Yearbook, 1961
items.description: The year the old village went under. On the last page, a speech, typed and pasted in.

effects.text: 'We will not pretend this is progress. We will say their names.' - O. Ottoline, Head Girl, 1961.

items.vagueText: A cracked leather yearbook. The last page has been read so many times it's soft.

items.name: Junie's Speech Notebook
items.description: Every family, every shop, the swimming hole, the stupid goose. Use it at the Last Assembly, once the stage is yours.

effects.text: You step up to the microphone and start with the first name.

terrains.name: Half-emptied Lockers
terrains.description: Doors hanging open, stickers peeling. Some still have stuff inside.

terrains.name: Stacked Moving Boxes
terrains.description: Labelled in marker: KITCHEN, MUM'S STUFF, DO NOT OPEN.

terrains.name: Freshly Mopped Floor
terrains.description: There is a yellow sign. Nobody reads the yellow sign.

terrains.name: Reservoir Seep
terrains.description: Cold water coming up between the floor tiles. The town is already going.

terrains.name: Vending Machine
terrains.description: The last fully stocked thing in Lowmoor. Bang it in the right place.

terrains.name: Trophy Case
terrains.description: County champions, 1987. Spelling bee, 2004. Best Kept Village, every year until this one.

effects.text: You take a photo of every trophy. Someone should remember.

terrains.name: Stage Spotlight
terrains.description: A pool of warm light on the assembly hall floor. Standing in it makes your heart go fast.

snack.label: can with a cartoon lightning bolt
clamshell box from the petrol station
cookie the size of your palm

note.label: note folded into a tiny star
sticky note with just a heart

areas.name: Monday: Lowmoor High
areas.description: Corridors half packed into boxes, noticeboards stripped to drawing pins. Water stains climbing the walls. Somewhere, the goose.
areas.transitionName: The bell rings. Survive until Wednesday.
areas.gmNotes: Establish the week: boxes, water stains, everyone leaving. Theo knows Rosalind has the notebook and is having a party on Wednesday. The janitor trades lost property for favours. Hall monitors give detention slips; three means going home.

areas.name: Wednesday: The Achterbergs' Empty House
areas.description: Rosalind's farewell party in a house that is mostly boxes and echoes. Fairy lights on bare walls. Music too loud. Your notebook is somewhere in here, and so is she.
areas.transitionName: Walk home along the levee. Friday's coming.
areas.gmNotes: Party energy curdled by goodbyes. Rosalind can be talked down rather than out-argued; when she cracks, she hands the notebook back and becomes friendly. Priya tags along and helps.

areas.name: Friday: The Last Assembly
areas.description: The assembly hall, chairs in rows, a banner reading #NEWBEGINNINGS over the stage. Water at the edges of the floor. Mags Calloway stands at the microphone.
areas.gmNotes: Final confrontation, verbal. Mags is not a villain; she is scared. Leaving her speechless and then giving the speech (using the notebook) wins. Nan Ottoline wants the old village named too.

goal.summary: Get your speech notebook back from Rosalind, out-talk Mags Calloway at Friday's Last Assembly, then give the farewell speech Lowmoor deserves.
goal.winText: You read every name. Every family, every shop, the swimming hole, Mrs. Pell's cookies, Theo Marsh who knew things, the stupid goose. It takes twelve minutes. Nobody leaves. When you finish, Nan Ottoline is the first one standing, and Mags Calloway is the second.
goal.lossText: Your mum picks you up early. You watch the school get smaller in the wing mirror, and the speech stays folded in your pocket, and on Saturday the water closes over all of it without anyone saying a word.

gm.persona: A narrator who remembers being sixteen: affectionate, sharp-eyed, never mocking the feelings, always noticing the water creeping in at the edges.
gm.voice: Present tense, second person. Specific details: brand-less snacks, stickers, the exact sound of lockers. Funny first, then gently sad.
threads: Everyone is moving somewhere different; this is the last week they will all be in one place.
Rosalind and Junie's friendship broke in Year 9 and neither will say why.
Nan Ottoline gave the farewell speech for the first village in 1961, and was cut off.
The water is already coming up through the floors.

fallback.intro: Five days until the floodgates close. Lowmoor High is half in boxes, the noticeboards are bare, and the only thing still fully stocked is the vending machine. You have one job this week: give the farewell speech at Friday's Last Assembly. Your notebook was in your bag at lunch. It isn't now.
areaEnter: Monday. The corridors smell of cardboard and floor polish. Somebody has drawn a fish on the water line on the wall.
Wednesday night. The bass from Rosalind's party shakes dust off the empty shelves. Fairy lights, bare walls, everyone pretending it's normal.
Friday. The assembly hall is full. The banner says #NEWBEGINNINGS. There is water around your shoes.
lowHp: Breathe. In for four, out for four. Like Coach said.
Your face is hot. Everyone is looking. Nobody is looking. Both feel true.
You could go home. Nobody would blame you. You'd blame you.
events: Somewhere a locker slams and the whole corridor jumps.
Every phone in the room buzzes at once. A photo of you is going round.
The goose appears at the end of the corridor. It is watching. It is always watching.
The lights flicker. Water ticks somewhere behind the walls.

audio.mood: bedroom-pop guitar, lo-fi drums, a cassette hiss; underneath, something like water moving
suggestions: Japanese Breakfast - Soft Sounds from Another Planet
Boards of Canada - Music Has the Right to Children
